title: Cleaning sequence
audience: Trainees and workers on the window cleaning (all heights) track, and quoting staff who estimate ground-based window jobs. Not a method for work at height.
learningOutcomes: Describe a safe top-to-bottom cleaning sequence for a ground-level window or panel.
Explain how a documented sequence supports quality, time estimates and a fair quote.
Identify the points at which the sequence must stop because the access or conditions have changed.

instruction.heading: Why sequence matters
instruction.body: A consistent cleaning sequence protects the glass, the frame, the public and the worker. It keeps wash water from running back over areas already cleaned, and it keeps the work area predictable. A written sequence is also the basis for a fair time estimate and a quote that reflects the actual work, which is why this lesson links method to revenue.

instruction.heading: Set up before the first pane
instruction.body: Confirm the scope, the exclusion zone and the wind and weather limits in the job plan. Check the survey sheet from the glass and frame survey for held panels, and do not clean any held panel. Set out the approved product, its safety data sheet and the equipment, and confirm the water supply and any pole is inspected. The set-up is complete when the supervisor has signed the job plan and the zone is marked.

instruction.heading: The top-to-bottom sequence
instruction.body: Work from the top of the panel down. Wet the surface from the top so the product and water run down through the dirt rather than being left to dry on the glass. Apply the approved product only where the method calls for it and only for the dwell time the product label or safety data sheet states. Agitate the surface with the approved tool, then rinse from the top down. Clean the frame and sill after the glass where the method requires it, so that frame runoff does not dirty the glass. Finish with a squeegee or dry cloth stroke that starts at the top edge and ends at the bottom edge.

instruction.heading: Checks during the work
instruction.body: Look at each pane after rinsing for streaks, residue and missed areas, and correct them before moving on. Check the exclusion zone and the wind between panels. If a pane shows a new crack, a loose frame or a change in the weather, stop, hold the pane and tell the supervisor. The sequence is only safe while the conditions match the job plan.

instruction.heading: Documenting the method and the time
instruction.body: Record the sequence used, the product name and the safety data sheet reference, the time taken per panel or elevation, and any panels that were held or excluded. These records support future quotes and show the customer what was done. They must be factual. Do not record a guaranteed finish or a result that was not inspected.

instruction.heading: Pricing and revenue
instruction.body: A documented sequence lets a business estimate time and materials with more consistency. A higher rate is supportable where the work is more complex, such as a difficult set-up, held panels that need extra coordination, or a large pole job that needs more inspection. Do not promise a rate or a result for work whose scope is not verified. Tie any price to the scope, the exclusions and the method. A quote becomes binding once accepted, and extra work outside it needs the client's approval (Western Australian consumer page, last updated 4 September 2026); the Northern Territory page (no date shown) sets the same rule.

instruction.heading: Limits and boundary
instruction.body: This lesson covers ground-level and ground-based cleaning only. It does not authorise work on a ladder, a platform or a roof. Where the sequence would need height, the job returns to the access decision in the scope lesson. Completing this lesson does not grant any licence or height authority.

procedure: Confirm the job plan, the wind limit and the exclusion zone, and check the survey sheet for held panels.
Inspect the equipment and confirm the approved product and its safety data sheet are on site.
Wet the surface from the top of the panel down.
Apply the approved product only as the label or safety data sheet directs, and agitate with the approved tool.
Rinse from the top down, keeping runoff out of stormwater (Queensland council page, last modified 22 July 2025: pressure-cleaning wastewater may not go into gutters or the stormwater system).
Check each pane for streaks, residue and missed areas, and correct before moving on.
Finish with a squeegee or dry cloth stroke from top to bottom.
Record the sequence, the product, the times, the held panels and any changes to the conditions.

workedExamples.situation: A ground-level shopfront has eight panels and a timber frame. One panel is marked as held after the survey because of a crack.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the sequence and the quote handle the held panel?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not clean the held panel. Keep it out of the sequence, record it as excluded with the reason, and state the exclusion in the quote. The remaining seven panels follow the top-to-bottom sequence. The record should show the held panel number and the decision owner, so the customer understands the exclusion.

workedExamples.situation: During the rinse of a ground-level window, a gust rises and the wash water starts to run onto a footpath.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the rinse, keep the public clear of the footpath, and check the wind against the job plan. Divert or collect the runoff as the plan requires, and do not discharge wash water to stormwater. Resume only when the wind is inside the plan and the runoff is controlled.

equipmentAndPpe: Approved product with its safety data sheet on site
Soft brush or approved cleaning tool and a clean water supply
Eye protection, gloves and non-slip footwear as specified in the job pack

commonErrors.error: Cleaning from the bottom up so that runoff dries on the glass.
commonErrors.prevention: Work from the top down and rinse from the top down.

commonErrors.error: Leaving product on the glass beyond the dwell time on the label.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the label and safety data sheet, and rinse at the stated time.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning a held panel because the customer asked for it.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep held panels out of the sequence and record the exclusion.

commonErrors.error: Quoting a guaranteed finish or rate for an unverified scope.
commonErrors.prevention: Tie each quote to the verified scope and state the exclusions.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Product labels and safety data sheets must be available for each approved product.
Runoff and stormwater: the Queensland council page says pressure-cleaning wastewater may not go into gutters or the stormwater system (last modified 22 July 2025).

Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to work at height, and it covers ground-level cleaning only. A boom-type platform needs a WP licence at a boom length of 11 metres or more in New South Wales, and a shorter boom may not need it there. In Queensland, platforms under 11 metres are not included in the WP licence definition. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there.

qualityStandard: The sequence runs from the top down and the rinse follows the same direction.
No held or excluded panel is cleaned, and every exclusion is recorded.
The product, its dwell time and its safety data sheet reference are recorded.
The quote reflects the verified scope and states its exclusions.
documentationEvidence: Sequence record with the product used and the safety data sheet reference
Time taken per panel or elevation
Held or excluded panels with the reason and the decision owner
Quote with the verified scope and exclusions
summary: A top-to-bottom sequence protects the glass, the frame and the public.
Follow the product label and the safety data sheet for every product.
Never clean a held panel, and record each exclusion.
Quote only the verified scope, and this lesson grants no height authority.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which direction should a ground-level window be cleaned and rinsed?
options: Bottom to top
Top to bottom
Side to side
Any direction

knowledgeChecks.question: A panel was held after the glass survey. What must happen to it during the clean?
options: It is cleaned last if time allows during the clean
It is cleaned gently by hand with a soft cloth and water
It is kept out of the sequence and the exclusion is recorded
It is cleaned with a stronger product for the whole job

knowledgeChecks.question: What governs how long a cleaning product is left on the glass?
options: The worker's experience on similar glass jobs
The customer's preference for the finish
The weather only, on the day of the job
The product label and safety data sheet

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a quote for a ground-level job be framed?
options: As tied to the verified scope, with exclusions stated
As a guaranteed finish at a fixed rate on the day
As a rate that ignores the held panels entirely
As a rate set by the height of the building

knowledgeChecks.question: The wind rises during a rinse and runoff heads toward a footpath. What is the first action?
options: Continue quickly to finish the rinse before the wind gets up more
Stop, keep the public clear, and control the runoff as the job plan requires
Turn the hose up to clear the footpath of the water very quickly
Move the work to the roof of the building next door on the day
